 Germany To Czechia: The Places Behind Shin Min-a & Ju Ji-hoon's 'The Remarried Empress'
 Where was 'The Remarried Empress' filmed? From Schleissheim Palace in Germany to Czech castles, here are the places behind the royal drama.
 By Esha Dasgupta 
 Published: Nov 14, 2026 10:00 AM IST 3 min read

 Highlights
 The Remarried Empress was shot across Germany and the Czech Republic, showcasing some of its most beautiful palaces, castles, and gardens.
 Check out everything you can see and do at these places, and how to get there.
 Since it began streaming on Disney+ on November 3, 2026, The Remarried Empress has drawn as much attention for its setting as for its story. Rather than move Empress Navier’s tale into a Korean historical backdrop, director Jo Soo-won kept the fictional Eastern Empire and Western Kingdom intact and took the cast to Europe, where real palaces and gardens stood in for the royal courts of the original web novel and webtoon. If you have seen the stunning backdrops of the show and are wondering where they actually are, here’s what we know about the shooting locations of The Remarried Empress .

 The Remarried Empress : Trailer, cast, and other details 
 The Remarried Empress follows Navier, the much-loved and admired Empress of the Eastern Empire, whose husband, Emperor Sovieshu, asks for a divorce after falling for the runaway slave Rashta. Navier agrees on one condition: approval to remarry Prince Heinrey of the Western Kingdom, leading to upheaval of all kinds. The cast includes Shin Min-a as Empress Navier Ellie Trovi, Ju Ji-hoon as Emperor Sovieshu Vict, Lee Jong-suk as Prince Heinrey Alles Lazlo, and Lee Se-young as Rashta Isqua. The supporting cast includes Lee Bong-ryun as Eliza, Choi Dae-hoon as Lord McKenna, Park Ho-san as Viscount Lotteshu, and Jung Young-joo as Albani, among others.

 The Remarried Empress shooting locations 
 Munich, Germany 
 Aerial view of Marienplatz with the New Town Hall in Munich | Image credit: Prakhyath DESHPANDE/Pexels 
 One of the main shooting locations of The Remarried Empress is Schleissheim Palace . It is located on the outskirts of Munich in Bavaria. Schleissheim Palace stood in for the imperial palace of the Eastern Empire, which is the backdrop for the court scenes at the centre of the story.
 Did you know?
 Schleissheim Palace became the main location after the production team scouted 16 European castles in person.
 Places to visit: Marienplatz, St. Peter’s Church, Viktualienmarkt, Hofbräuhaus München, Frauenkirche, Englischer Garten, Munich Residenz, and Nymphenburg Palace.
 Advertisement 
 How to reach: Munich International Airport is located within the city and about 26 kilometres from Schleissheim Palace.
 Czechia 
 Prague Castle at twilight, Czechia | Image credit: SHAHBAZ ZAMAN/Pexels 
 Czechia was a major shooting location for The Remarried Empress . The May Garden in Kroměříž provided the setting where the bond between Navier and Prince Heinrey slowly deepens. The crew also lined up the old lanes of Kutná Hora with shops carrying Korean-language signs, so European facades and Korean lettering sit side by side. Other important shooting locations across the country included several castles and gardens, such as the May Garden in Kroměříž, Hrádek u Nechanic chateau, Jaroměřice nad Rokytnou Castle, Tochovice Castle, Švihov Water Castle, and Červená Lhota Castle.
 Advertisement 
 Places to visit: Prague for its Gothic and Baroque architecture, Kutná Hora for the macabre Sedlec Ossuary, Karlovy Vary for its colonnades and mineral hot springs, and Brno for its modern architecture, cafe culture, and Špilberk Castle.
 How to reach: Václav Havel Airport Prague, Brno–Tuřany Airport, Leoš Janáček Airport Ostrava, and Pardubice Airport are the main airports serving Czechia.
